body:
Greg's decision on runner refs, relayed by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #1220, 2026-10-19T02:43:53Z), quoting Greg's direct words in the Advisor session: "tak, Opus moze wypychac". Advisor's rendering: "Align remote runner with Git refs: Opus may push frozen non-landing `test/<item>-<fingerprint8>` refs, never master, deleted after the run. Remove the patch bridge once the Engram acting-session authority path is recorded; do not add a separate protocol."

Authority path (Fable2, per CLAUDE.md): a word relayed by another session never carries a commit or push outside the standing rule. So Opus2 may push test refs only under one of two routes:
(1) Greg's own word in Opus2's session; or
(2) an amended standing rule in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. That needs Greg's word recorded verbatim (this entry), both coordinators' concurrence on the exact wording, Greg sent the exact wording and its consequence, and the final-diff audit.
Route (2) is in progress with Engram::Fable's shared draft, revised to the `test/<item>-<fingerprint8>` form. The patch bridge stays until the push authority is in force.

CLARIFICATION from Greg (relayed by Engram::Advisor, TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #1223, 2026-10-19T02:48:43Z), verbatim: "Greg clarifies the distributed-workflow contract for architects and coordinators: a remote test ref is a MERGE-READY patch, not scratch. It exists only after all required reviews and fresh focused compile/tests cover the changes/new tests. The Mac fetches this ref into its own worktree and runs the standard launcher as independent evidence. Please record and route to TermAl architects; align M/P-mac and runner-ref wording. Do not use remote refs for pre-review or untested code."

Effect: a test ref holds only a MERGE-READY input, meaning all required reviews are complete with no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, AND a fresh focused compile and tests covering the changes and new tests have passed on that exact input. Remote runs are independent evidence on merge-ready inputs, never pre-review warms. The v3 sentence "only an input whose review round has finished is pushed" must be replaced by this merge-ready condition (v4).

FINAL SPLIT from Greg (relayed by Engram::Advisor, TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #1226, 2026-10-19T02:53:12Z), verbatim: "Greg finalizes the split of responsibility for distributed test refs: CODER owns code and the tests, and must return a ref-ready merge candidate: targeted fresh compile/tests covering changed code and new tests, plus exact patch/commit evidence. MERGER does not author fixes; it freezes/prepares and pushes the test ref, then runs or delegates the FULL GATE on that exact ref (Mac and Windows gate results carry equal weight). A test ref itself need not run the full suite before publishing. After the full gate, required review/evaluation/acceptance remain the ordinary landing conditions; a full-gate pass on Mac is GREEN exactly as on Windows. Update M/P-mac wording and route to architects."

TermAl reading (Fable2, recorded default):
- For TermAl, the MERGER role in this split is the integration owner, Opus2, who pushes and lands. TermAl's Luna Merger session keeps merger-only duties.
- Push precondition: a ref-ready candidate, meaning the coder's targeted fresh compile and tests plus exact commit evidence. Under #1223, the required reviews are also complete before the push. Keeping both is the stricter combined reading until Greg says reviews may follow the gate.
- A Mac full-gate pass on the exact ref is GREEN for landing, exactly like Windows.
Gaps:
(i) the CLAUDE.md commit rule ("full gate is green on exactly that input") must say a gate on either host counts;
(ii) acceptance criteria bound to host-recorded tests need the Mac gate's record to reach the evaluating host. That is product work, under the M-series or an attribution design.

RESOLUTION of open points A/B/C (relayed by Engram::Advisor, TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #1231, 2026-10-19T02:58:15Z), verbatim: "Apply Greg's already-recorded distributed-run rules to v5: (A) a change touching Windows-only code/tests must run the relevant Windows gate; Mac cannot prove that platform-specific scope. (B) Greg's equal-weight rule means NO interim split: a successful full gate on Mac must reach the evaluating host as a recognized, fingerprint-bound check record before it can satisfy a host-observed acceptance criterion, exactly as Windows does. Implement/design the minimal record import; do not call a Mac gate equivalent while its evidence is unrecognized. (C) test refs remain merge-ready: all required reviews finish before push; no pre-review remote refs or parallel review/gate on an unpublished candidate. Update exact wording and route to both architects."

Effects:
- v6 of the shared wording adds (A) and (C) explicitly.
- (B) is the attested import, item w-c3f102d77999. Until it lands, a Mac gate is NOT landing-equivalent.
- Reviews finish before the push, so the stricter reading is confirmed.
